title: Partial versus total derivative of the historical q_u response
question: Is production dq_u/dH=+u/dt the total derivative of historical q_u across the flux-driven predictor family, or the partial derivative of an affine extension with q_bot and u held fixed?
production_affine_slope: partial q_u / partial H_end_cm at fixed u and q_bot = +u/dt_day
predictor_family_identity: u = dt_day/(dH_end_cm/dq_bot), hence dq_bot/dH_end_cm = u_FD/dt_day and approximately u/dt_day on E4 predictor plateaus

fixed_primary_case.selection_reason: These scales belong to the already-qualified E4 B3 u_FD plateau region. The 1e-4 fraction is excluded because E4 itself records a pathological wrong-sign u_FD there; no new selection is made from MAP07 output.

outputs: reconstructed q_u at each plus/minus predictor point using that point's u_A_point
finite-difference total dq_u/dH_cm along the predictor family
ratio total slope / production partial slope
frozen-u decomposition (u_A-u_FD)/dt showing first-order cancellation of +u/dt and dq_bot/dH
interpretation_rules: A near-zero total derivative does not make the production slope mathematically wrong; it establishes that the production slope is a partial affine-extension derivative, not the total derivative of q_u across neighboring predictor states.
Do not identify either derivative with physical bottom exchange without the separate MAP02/MAP03 corrector and mass-ledger evidence.
Use MAP03 to distinguish physical storage sensitivity (+u in the simple fixture) from bottom-outward exchange sensitivity (-u).
No production change follows from this retrospective diagnostic alone.
forbidden: no post-hoc replacement of E4 plateau selection
do not use the B3 1e-4 flux fraction as primary evidence
do not call the partial-versus-total distinction a defect without an explicit coupling-contract requirement
